entries: ALLOT'TERY is used by Shakespeare for allotment; but is not authorized by usage.
AP'OGRAPH noun [Gr.] An exemplar; a copy or transcript.

BESOT'verb intransitive [be and sot.] To make sottish; to infatuate; to stupify; to make dull or senseless.

1. To make to dote.

BIRDSTARES and BIRDSTONGUE; names of plants.

BIRD'-WITTED, adjective Not having the faculty of attention.

COUNTERWORK. [See Work.] To work in opposition to; to counteract; to hinder any effect by contrary operations.

That counterworks each folly and caprice.
FI'AT. [Latin from fio.] Let it be done; a decree; a command to do something.
MISSPELL'. verb transitive To spell wrong; to write or utter with wrong letters.
SELF-PARTIAL'ITY; noun [self and partiality.] That partiality by which a man overrates his own worth when compared with others.
SENSELESSLY adverb sens'lessly. In a senseless manner; stupidly; unreasonably; as a man senselessly arrogant.

SHORN participle passive of shear.

1. Cut off; as a lock of wool shorn.

2. Having the hair or wool cut off or sheared; as a shorn lamb.

3. Deprived; as a prince shorn of his honors.
UN'ARM verb transitive To disarm; to strip of armor or arms. [Not used. See Disarm.]

UNDERPROP' verb transitive To support; to uphold.

And underprop the head that bears the crown.

UNRECLA'IMED. adjective

1. Not reclaimed; not brought to a domestic state; not tamed; as a wild beast unreclaimed

2. Not reformed; not called back from vice to virtue.
